subject: biology
title: Indicator species
key_idea: An **indicator species** is an organism whose presence or absence shows how polluted an environment is. Some species need clean conditions. Others can live where there is pollution. Scientists use them as evidence of pollution levels.

sections.heading: Indicator species for water and air

blocks.text: (Separate science) Some organisms are found only in clean places and some only in polluted ones. This section covers the main indicator species.

items.meaning: A species whose presence or absence shows the level of pollution in an area.
Harmful substances released into the water or air.

diagram.alt: Pick an indicator species to see what it shows about pollution and why.
diagram.prompt: Pick an indicator species you find

options.label: Freshwater shrimp
results: Freshwater shrimps are not found in polluted water

options.label: Stonefly
results: Stoneflies are clean water indicators and are not found in polluted water

options.label: Sludgeworm
results: Sludgeworms are found where the oxygen concentration is low

options.label: Bloodworm
results: Bloodworms in a pond show that the water is polluted

options.label: Lichen
results: Lichens are sensitive to air pollution, so mostly sensitive species means low pollution

options.label: Blackspot fungus on roses
results: Blackspot fungus will not grow where there is a high concentration of sulfur dioxide

items: Freshwater shrimp and stonefly indicate clean water. Sludgeworm and bloodworm indicate polluted water.
Lichens and blackspot fungus are indicators of air pollution, not water pollution.

blocks.text: Pollution such as sewage lowers the oxygen concentration in water. Species then survive or disappear according to how much oxygen they need.

items: Sewage increases the number of aerobic bacteria, which use oxygen from the water in respiration.
Sewage can also block light or kill plants, so less oxygen is made by photosynthesis.
Where the oxygen concentration is high, more organisms can survive and respire, so biodiversity is higher.
Where the oxygen concentration is low, only species such as sludgeworms survive.
Sewage lowers oxygen because bacteria respire and photosynthesis falls.
Biodiversity is highest where the oxygen concentration is highest.

blocks.text: To evaluate the use of indicator species, look at what they show and what they cannot show.

rows: Simple: finding the species in a sample shows the level of pollution
Shows that an area is polluted, not which pollutant caused it
Linked to measured data, such as a low oxygen concentration
The right species must be identified correctly
Species that are absent from an area give evidence that it is polluted
A species could be absent for another reason, so use other evidence too

items: Indicator species give evidence of pollution levels.
They are stronger evidence when they agree with measurements such as oxygen concentration.

checks.q: Give the names of two indicator species that provide evidence for clean water.
Rose plants near a factory are not infected with blackspot fungus. State why.
checks.a: Blackspot fungus will not grow where there is a high concentration of sulfur dioxide.

checks.q: Explain why sewage pollution in a river can decrease the oxygen levels in the water.
checks.a: Sewage increases the number of aerobic bacteria, which use oxygen from the water in respiration. Sewage can also stop plants getting light, so there is less photosynthesis and less oxygen produced.

exam_phrases: stonefly and freshwater shrimp provide evidence for clean water
lichen is an air pollution indicator
blackspot fungus will not grow where areas have high sulfur dioxide
oxygen concentration is highest here so organisms can survive / respire
increased levels of (aerobic) bacteria use oxygen from the water in respiration
prevent plants from getting light so no oxygen produced by photosynthesis

mistakes.wrong: Lichens show that a river is polluted.
mistakes.right: Lichens are an air quality indicator, not a water quality indicator.

mistakes.wrong: Freshwater shrimps and stoneflies live in polluted water.
mistakes.right: They are not found in polluted water. They are clean water indicators.

mistakes.wrong: Sewage lowers the oxygen because it is full of bacteria.
mistakes.right: Explain the link: the bacteria respire and use oxygen from the water, or sewage prevents plants getting light so no oxygen is produced by photosynthesis.

worked_example.question:
A fertiliser factory releases waste into a stream. Samples of water were taken at five points, A, B, C, D and E, along the stream.

Point along stream | Oxygen concentration (ppm)
A | 1.5
B | 2.7
C | 3.4
D | 4.4
E | 4.5

Explain where the biodiversity will be highest in the stream.
answer_points: The biodiversity will be highest at point D to E, the points furthest from the factory.
This is because the oxygen concentration is highest there.
So organisms can survive and respire.
worked_example.tip: Name the place, then link it to the oxygen concentration, then to survival or respiration.
